html:
Ubangi-Shari was the French colony that became the Central African Republic, created in 1903 and joined to French Equatorial Africa in 1910.

France did not pay to run it. Most land was handed to concession companies that forced people to gather wild rubber and later to grow cotton, with beatings and hostages taken from villages. Men were also sent to build the Congo to Ocean railway. Sleeping sickness and famine cut the population.

Resistance, above all the Kongo-Wara rebellion, was crushed. The colony left little in schools or roads when Barthélemy Boganda led it toward self-rule in 1958, which helps explain how weak the state has been since.
sum: Ubangi-Shari was the French colony that became the Central African Republic, created in 1903 and joined to French Equatorial Africa in 1910.
